questions.q: What's the tradeoff between full reprocessing and incremental processing?
options: Full reprocessing is simple and always correct but wasteful at scale; incremental is faster and cheaper but requires knowing what "new" means
Full reprocessing is always faster than incremental processing
Incremental processing never actually works correctly with Delta tables
There's no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Full reprocessing reads the entire bronze table every run; incremental reads only what's actually new.

questions.q: What is a watermark, in the context of incremental processing?
options: A stored value — like the latest already-processed timestamp — used to filter for only newer data
A visual overlay added to a dashboard
A Unity Catalog permission level
A type of Delta table constraint
questions.explain: This is the mechanism behind the pattern of filtering bronze for only rows newer than the last processed value.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 26's _ingested_at metadata column matter for the watermark pattern?
options: Without it, there'd be no reliable way to tell old bronze rows from new ones at all
It has no real connection to watermarking
It's only used for Unity Catalog audit logging
It's required only when using Change Data Feed, not watermarks
questions.explain: This metadata column, added in Lesson 26, exists specifically to make this incremental pattern possible.

questions.q: What does Delta's Change Data Feed (CDF) provide that a manual watermark doesn't?
options: Precise, row-level tracking of exactly which rows were inserted, updated, or deleted between two versions, directly from the transaction log
CDF and watermarks are functionally identical in every way
CDF only works on tables without a transaction log
CDF replaces the need for any Delta table at all
questions.explain: CDF must be explicitly enabled per table, but is a more precise incremental signal than a watermark column.

questions.q: What's the natural next step this chapter is heading toward after covering watermarks and CDF?
options: Autoloader and Structured Streaming — processing new files continuously as they arrive, rather than in scheduled batches
Going back to full reprocessing for simplicity
Moving on to Unity Catalog governance entirely
Abandoning incremental processing altogether
questions.explain: This is exactly what Lessons 32-34 introduce, once "process only what's new" becomes the actual goal.
